abstract: A common feature of neurodegeneration is selective vulnerability, where certain neurons succumb to disease, while others remain spared. The molecular underpinnings of these differences remain elusive. Here, we use single-nucleus RNA-sequencing to investigate transcriptional alterations in the motor cortex of a mouse model of Huntington's disease (HD), a movement disorder caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the Huntingtin gene. We observe transcriptomic separation of HD and control samples within the vulnerable glutamatergic, but not disease-resistant GABAergic cell clusters. Gene expression changes follow a two-stage trajectory with distinct early and late-stage changes. Gene co-expression network analysis reveals a gene module with putative neuroprotective properties. Analysis of differentially expressed genes furthermore demonstrates progressive dysregulation of neuronal cell-type identity and upregulation of ER-phagy receptors. Mechanistic investigations in cellular HD models point to increased ER-phagy. Taken together, these findings advance our understanding of neuronal vulnerability, and suggest a role for ER-phagy in HD.
